questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to a European and English-speaking country - preferably in the EU. That excluded pretty much everything but Ireland. Furthermore, Ireland is just such a nice country with really friendly people:) I'd heard that Cork was a really great student city so it just seemed perfect.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit difficult to get the courses/modules I wanted but apart from the administrative part of it, it was AMAZING.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, the International Office at UCC hosts webinars prior to arrivals, and are good at emailing information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive anything (personally) apart from the offer to have a meeting with the International Office in addition to the orientations that they host. I also didn't need anything but was aware that assistance would be given upon request.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy for me as I lived with a family member of a friend that I knew prior to my exchange. I would recommend joining Facebook or WhatsApp groups as it is quite difficult to get if you don't have a direct connection.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Buses are quite unreliable so be careful about living too far from campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really happy in my housing but generally the housing available to students is way too expensive and usually not in the best conditions:(

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't really remember, so it must have been fairly easy:) Just make sure to check your UCPH e-mail and your UCC e-mail regularly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Office at both UCPH and UCC.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. I ended up getting some fine classes but had to redo my registration multiple times as some classes weren't available. This is made more difficult as you have to make your entire timetable work by yourself and can have no overlaps. There is a website that is made available for this a couple of weeks before the semester starts but prepare to redo it when you are rejected from specific classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a plan A, B, C, D and E about the classes you want as they can be quite difficult to get a spot in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I'd generally recommend doing 4th year courses rather than 3rd year (even if you're just a 3rd year) as this level is more suitable. Some classes were easier than others and the general level was a bit lower than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCC: more memorization, more lectures rather than group work and handwritten exams. But it worked fairly well and the lecturers are really good.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MB4019: Computational Biology
BC4001: Advanced Cell Biology
BC3021: Cell Signalling in Health and Disease
MB3007: Molecular Genetics and Genomics
NT2013: Fundamentals of Nutrition
HI1115: Modern Irish History for Visiting Students

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I'd recommend MB4019 as an introduction to bioinformatics. It is nice background knowledge to have. 
The lecturer in BC4001 is really good but the material is similar to what I had had at UCPH. 
I cannot recommend NT2013 as the course is not well-structured...
HI1115 was quite interesting:)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing is really expensive (1000 euros is not unusual for student housing), so I was very lucky but was very surprised at the general housing prices.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out was more expensive than expected. Public transport was less expensive that expected (please get the Student Leap Card!!!)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many clubs and societies!!! Literally amazing.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything. More than 200 clubs/societies with all types of activities/sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fáilte Refugees Society is a really cool charity society. The boxing club is really good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the nature of Ireland! Grab a pint at the local pub and listen to some traditional music:)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Irish people are very friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs/societies and don't be afraid to speak!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, I really enjoy the company of Irish people:) I was really confused about how they drive on the left side of the road though.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their "easygoingness."

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Join clubs
2. Beware of your timetable
3. Don't be scared if your housing seems expensive (it's probably just normal...)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join the Erasmus Network and the International Students group chats as quickly as possible as they do cool activities all throughout the semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting all the administrative stuff done

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
